Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Apollo Hospital to Offer Treatment Discounts
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Indraprastha Medical Corporation Limited to provide special healthcare discounts to its customers. Under the agreement, bank clients can receive a 10% discount on inpatient room charges, preventive health check packages, and attendees’ health checkups, along with a 5% discount on outpatient investigations.
Additional benefits include complimentary registration, access to the international patient lounge, and transportation from the New Delhi airport to the hotel or hospital for patients booking through the Apollo Information Center in Kathmandu. Customers must make payments using the bank’s debit or credit cards to avail these services, with the partnership aimed at making quality medical treatment more accessible and affordable.

Headline: NRB Takes Action Against Three Major Banks for Rule Violations
Full Content:
The Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken formal action against three of the country's leading commercial banks
NIC Asia Bank
,
Global IME Bank
, and
Nepal Investment Mega Bank
following reports of regulatory misconduct.
The penalties, which range from heavy cash fines to formal warnings for top executives, were issued after the central bank’s review of the second quarter of the current fiscal year (2082/83).

Failure to maintain adequate loan loss provisions (ageing-wise) and non-compliance with loan rescheduling/restructuring rules. Additionally, the core banking software allowed for the re-creation of settled loans using old value dates.

Board of Directors and CEO
Formal Caution
Violations including: disbursing loans without customer signatures on security documents, lending beyond collateral limits, maintaining interest rate differences of over 2% for similar loan types, and using new short-term loans for debt recovery in violation of working capital guidelines.

The central bank revealed that these issues were not just found in paperwork but were confirmed during physical inspections. For
Global IME Bank
, the NRB conducted a specific
on-site monitoring
visit at their head office. During this visit, inspectors discovered a technical loophole in the bank’s computer system that allowed old, settled loans to be "re-created," potentially hiding the true status of unpaid debts.
Speaking on these developments, the
Spokesperson of NRB, Mr. Guru Prasad Paudel
, clarified that the central bank is simply enforcing the law to protect the stability of the financial system.
"These actions were taken based on the specific details and data provided by the banks to the NRB," said Mr. Paudel. Such actions are mandatory for any bank that violates the rules and laws set forth in the NRB Act.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Limited Launches ‘Saathi Ghar Karja’ Scheme with 6.99% Interest
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has introduced the “NIC Asia Saathi Ghar Karja” scheme to help customers fulfill their housing needs by offering home loans of up to Rs. 10 crore.
The loan carries a fixed interest rate of 6.99% for seven years and can be used for buying a house or apartment, constructing or reconstructing a home, and purchasing land.
Loans range from a minimum of Rs. 25 lakh to a maximum tenure of 25 years, with up to 80% financing for first-time homebuyers and 70% for others. Customers under this scheme will also receive a lifetime free credit card service.

Full Content:

announces it will not distribute dividends for the Fiscal Year 2081/82.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank on recovery path to reclaim glorious past
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank, one of Nepal's top Class A commercial banks, which previously suffered setbacks, is now on the rapid recovery phase to reclaim its strong market position.
Following its aggressive expansion, the bank is now focused on consolidation, asset quality improvement and consolidating its capital base.
Key strategies include changes in top management, speedy digitization, downsizing branches and the proposal of right shares issuance to increase capital. Early indications show that the bank is on the right track.
"Since all bank and financial institutions are facing difficulties right now due to the country's overall economy situation, our bank is no exception. However, we are working tirelessly to recover," Jayendra Rawal, the bank's Chief Information Officer.
According to him, the bank has now adopted a more defensive strategy for a sustainable growth by prioritizing loan restructuring and recovery, gradual business expansion, full-fledged digitization and portfolio diversification.
The bank has diversified its portfolios in corporate and energy sectors. It has invested millions of rupees in these sectors.
To consolidate the capital structure, maintain capital adequacy ratios and expand future business, the bank has recently proposed a 50 percent right share issuance on the basis of 2:1 ratio (one new share for every two existing shares), aiming to raise Rs 7.45 billion from the issuance of the total 74,587,835 units. Upon the completion of the issuance, the bank's paid up capital will rise from existing Rs 14.91 billion to Rs 22.37 billion. However, the proposal is subject to approve by Nepal Rastra Bank, Nepal's regulatory body for Banks and Financial Institutions (BFIs).
Similarly, the bank has proposed to issue Perpetual Non-Cumulative Preference Shares worth Rs 5 billion at a face value of Rs 100 per unit, aiming to strengthen the bank's capital base and manage capital pressure.
"The bank's move is to inject the raised capital to boost absorbing equity and investment loans," said Rawal.
The bank is also working to go fully digitized and make its branch network effective in a bid to minimize operational costs and increase efficiency.
Bank's glorious past and challenges
The bank was formed in 2013 through the merger of NIC Bank and Bank of Asia Nepal. The first-ever merger set a precedent for future merger in Nepal's banking sector. The bank's sustained and high quality performance was recognized as the Bank of the Year Nepal by The Banker in 2007 and 2013.
Until some years ago, the bank stood out as one of the leading banks in Nepal with the expansion of over 350 branches, and over 100 extension counters. It also operated 41 branchless banking services and more than 470 ATMs.
It also pioneered in introducing digital-first services with the NIC MoApp (mobile banking) and iServe (a platform for all digital services). By 2022, It served more than 3 million customers until 2022, positioning itself as one of the best banks in terms of overall financial health.
The bank also established its subsidiaries, including NIC Asia Capital Limited and NIC Asia Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited.
However, the bank faced challenges in recovering loans following the country's economic slowdown especially in the aftermath of Covid-19 pandemic. Alleged attacks tarnished its image, adding to its woes.
Despite these odds, the bank has maintained stability and is now on the recovery path. According to Its Q2, 2082/83 financial report, its total loans and advances to customers stood at Rs 223.98 billion while deposits from customers grew to Rs 333.78 billion, 6.33 percent up from Rs 313.91 billion in the same corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Similarly, its reserves increased to Rs 22.06 billion from Rs 19.81 billion in the previous year. Its net worth per share is Rs 198.33.
"We have now attracted around 4 million customers now," said Rawal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Awards Scholarships to Talented Underprivileged Students Across Nepal
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has started providing scholarships to 75 talented students from underprivileged, marginalized, and differently-abled backgrounds studying in grades 6–10 at government and community schools outside the Kathmandu Valley.
The initiative, part of the bank’s CSR program, aims to enhance educational quality, support personality development, and encourage continued learning. The bank has also previously contributed by building libraries in schools across all seven provinces.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Launches Attractive Gold Loan Scheme with Competitive Interest Rates
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank, moving forward with the slogan “Bank Pani, Sathi Pani, Ramro Pani, Hamro Pani,” has launched an attractive Gold Loan scheme offering competitive interest rates with a 1–3% premium facility.
Under this scheme, customers can obtain loans up to NPR 50 lakh by pledging gold bars or jewelry, receiving 70–80% of the market value.
The loan can also be used for purchasing jewelry. To ensure smooth service and address customer queries effectively, the bank has established a dedicated ‘Loan Assistance Center’ at designated branches.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank and SuryaJyoti Life Insurance Partner to Offer Lifetime Free Credit Cards
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank and SuryaJyoti Life Insurance Company have entered into a strategic partnership to provide lifetime free credit card services to SuryaJyoti Life’s insured customers and insurance agents. The memorandum of understanding was signed in Kathmandu by the Chief Executive Officers of both institutions.
Under this agreement, eligible customers and agents will be able to obtain credit cards without any annual fees, making it easier to manage emergency financial needs and access digital payment facilities. The bank believes this collaboration will further support financial inclusion and help integrate SuryaJyoti Life’s customers and agents into the digital economy by offering more convenient and accessible banking services.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Launches Online Portal for Auction of Banking and Non-Banking Assets
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) has launched an online portal to provide detailed information on the auction sale of its banking assets, non-banking assets, and properties held as collateral. Through this portal, customers can access comprehensive details of auctioned properties, including plot numbers, area, photos, maps, and location information via Google Maps by scanning the QR code published in auction notices or directly visiting the portal.
The platform also allows interested buyers to send inquiries by submitting their contact details through a message box provided for each property. The bank stated that the portal will be regularly updated with information on assets available for auction and related notices, enabling potential buyers to conveniently obtain complete and reliable information online.

Headline: Ms. Anupa Pradhan Rajbhandari Appointed as  Director of NIC Asia Bank
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited has appointed Ms. Anupa Pradhan Rajbhandari as a director representing the general public shareholders. With nearly three decades of experience in the banking sector, Ms. Rajbhandari brings extensive professional expertise to the board.
The newly appointed director took the oath of office and confidentiality from Board Chairman Mr. Ashok Kumar Agrawal. She holds a master’s degree in Business Administration and previously served in leadership roles across various departments at the former Bank of Kathmandu.
Extending best wishes for her successful tenure, the bank family has warmly welcomed and congratulated Ms. Rajbhandari on her appointment.

Headline: NIC Asia Urges Customers to Update PAN and Email Details
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited has requested its customers to update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) and email address in their bank accounts to ensure proper tax record management and smoother banking services. The bank stated that PAN is mandatory for recording interest tax deductions in the government’s E-TDS system as per the Income Tax Act 2058.
Customers can update their PAN through the bank’s online portal, NIC ASIA MoBank app, or by visiting any branch office. Once PAN is updated, tax deduction details will be automatically reflected in the income tax system, making it easier for customers to obtain tax certificates without visiting the bank.
Similarly, customers are encouraged to update their email address via the bank’s website, mobile banking app, or branches to receive timely banking communications. The bank has also advised customers to contact nearby branches or customer service centers if previous PAN or email updates were not properly recorded.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Offers 30% Discount on Locker Services
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has increased the special discount on its locker services to 30%, allowing customers to securely store their valuable items and important documents. The offer is valid until 6th Magh 2082 and applies to the first-year annual fee.
The bank provides lockers in various sizes across its branches nationwide, ensuring customers can safely keep their belongings. This enhanced discount aims to make locker services more convenient, accessible, and affordable for all customers.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Condemns Misconduct at Itahari Branch, Seeks Legal Action for Staff Safety
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has expressed serious concern over an incident at its Itahari branch, where an individual entered the premises with malicious intent and engaged in abusive and disorderly behavior against bank employees. The bank stated that such unlawful and disruptive acts in sensitive service-providing institutions are unacceptable and have created an atmosphere of insecurity for both staff and the overall banking sector.
The bank highlighted that activities such as vandalism, threats to life and property, and the use of highly flammable substances within bank premises not only endanger employees but also negatively impact the nation’s financial system and workplace safety. NIC Asia Bank has urged the concerned authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and take legal action against those involved, while also ensuring the safety and security of bank offices and their employees.

Full Content:

has proposed to issue rights shares to its shareholders in a 2:1 ratio, equivalent to a 50% rights offering. The bank has formally requested prior approval from Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) to issue rights shares.

Full Content:

Debit and credit card users of NIC Asia Bank will receive up to 10% discount on various IME Hospitality hotels, restaurants, and cable car services, including Hotel Le Himalaya, Ila Hotels, The Lakeside Resort, Sake & Feng Restaurant, Maulakali, and Lumbini Cable Cars.
The offer aims to promote digital payment and cashless transactions.

Headline: Ashok Kumar Agrawal Appointed Chairman of NIC Asia Bank
Full Content:

His appointment is effective from today, and he has taken the oath of office and secrecy from Nepal Rastra Bank Governor Prof. Dr. Biswo Nath Poudel.
With extensive experience in banking, finance, insurance, and the corporate sector, Mr. Agrawal is expected to provide strong leadership and contribute significantly to the bank’s continued growth and Nepal’s economic development.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Launches Online Portal for Auction Property Information
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank Limited has launched an online portal to provide detailed information on bank-owned, non-banking, and collateral-backed properties available for auction. Headline: Bank Employees’ Union Condemns Violence Against JBBL Staff, Calls for Zero Tolerance and Strong Action
Full Content:
The NIC Asia Bank Employees’ Union has strongly condemned an incident in which employees of Jyoti Bikash Bank Limited, while performing official loan recovery duties, were subjected to inhuman, humiliating, and unlawful behavior by some borrowers in a public place. The union stated that such violence and public humiliation against bank employees carrying out lawful duties is a direct attack on the banking system, the rule of law, and financial discipline.
It warned that continued inaction by authorities could seriously affect employee safety, morale, and public trust in the banking sector. The union has urged the government, regulators, security agencies, and banking associations to take immediate and effective action, ensure employee protection, punish the виновी parties, and adopt a zero-tolerance policy against violence toward bank staff.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Kartik; GBIME Tops the Charts
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the fourth month of the fiscal year 2082/83, ending in Kartik.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 19.37 Arba. Global IME Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 2.51 Arba, overtaking Nabil Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 2.46 Crores. Prime Commercial Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 1.58 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and NMB Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Citizens Bank International recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 1.64 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 1.79 Arba, despite eight out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Garima Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 39.77 Crores, outpacing Garima Bikas Bank, Muktinath Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 38.42 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 30.25 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Miteri Development Bank and Green Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 3.5 Crores and Rs. 2.18 Crores, respectively.
Furthermore, seven banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, Salapa, Lumbini Bikas Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Offers 15% Discount on Locker Services for Secure Storage
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank is offering a special 15% discount on the first-year annual fee for its locker services, allowing customers to securely store valuable items and important documents.
The service is available in various sizes across 150 branches nationwide, making it easier and more convenient for customers to safeguard their belongings.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Customers to Receive Special Discounts at Drishti Eye Care
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed an agreement with Drishti Eye Care, enabling its customers to receive up to 20% discounts on various medical services when making digital payments.
The offer includes discounts on ENT and general services, 20% on OPD and 10% on investigations, and multiple eye-care services such as 20% off general OPD, 5% off surgeries and operations, 10% off laboratory services, and 7.5% off optical products.
Customers can avail these benefits by paying through NIC Asia’s debit, credit, or prepaid cards, or via the MoBank app. The bank believes this collaboration will support customers' healthcare needs while promoting digital payments and cashless transactions in Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with NCHL to Launch NEPALPAY Card for Enhanced Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed a strategic agreement with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to issue NEPALPAY Cards to its customers, aiming to strengthen the country’s payment system. The agreement was signed by CEO Sujit Kumar Shakya on behalf of the bank and CEO Nilesh Man Singh Pradhan for NCHL. Under this partnership, NIC Asia Bank becomes a key partner in NCHL’s Domestic Card Scheme and the National Card Switch (NPS-NCS).
The initiative enables the bank to fully integrate with Nepal’s national payment switch and issue the NEPALPAY Card, ensuring transactions through POS and ATM networks follow a standardized national fee structure. This move provides customers access to modern, reliable, and nationally recognized domestic card services, reinforcing the bank’s commitment to digital banking. NIC Asia Bank expects that the NEPALPAY Card will expand financial inclusion, promote cashless transactions, and contribute to the growth of Nepal’s digital economy.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Customers to Receive Discounts at Chiropractic and Manual Therapy Centre
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with Chiropractic and Manual Therapy Centre to offer its customers up to 10% discount on services at branches in Baluwaatar, Tripureshwor, Kathmandu, and Butwal.
Customers can avail the discount by paying digitally using the bank’s debit, credit, prepaid cards, or MoBank app. The collaboration aims to support customers’ healthcare needs while promoting digital and cashless payments in Nepal.

Headline: NIC ASIA Bank Launches Competitive Share-Backed Loan to Boost Investor Liquidity
Full Content:
NIC ASIA Bank has introduced a Share-Backed Loan facility that allows investors to borrow against their existing NEPSE-listed shares without selling them. The product offers fast service, transparent processing, and flexible repayment options with a maximum tenure of one year.
The loan features competitive pricing, including a 9.50% fixed rate option and a floating rate with zero premium over the bank’s base rate, making it a cost-effective borrowing choice. Investors can borrow up to 70% of the value of their pledged shares, based on the lower of the current market price or the 180-day average price, as per Nepal Rastra Bank guidelines.
The facility is available through both Demand Loan (DL) and Overdraft (OD) options, with loan amounts ranging from NPR 5 million to NPR 120 million. Eligible applicants must be between 21 and 70 years old and comply with the bank’s fee structure.
With this offering, NIC ASIA aims to support active investors by providing modern, flexible financing aligned with capital market needs and long-term wealth-building goals.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Appoints New CIO and CGO to Strengthen Digital Services and Customer Protection
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has restructured its senior management by appointing new executives to the roles of Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Chief Grievance Officer (CGO), effective November 19. The changes reflect the bank’s focus on enhancing digital infrastructure, transparency, and customer service.
Assistant CEO Jayendra Rawal has been promoted to CIO, where he will lead IT operations, digital banking strategy, cybersecurity, and official information communication. He can be contacted at 9851231332 or 01-5970101.
Similarly, COO and Company Secretary Kamal Khadka has been appointed as CGO, placing customer grievance handling at a high operational level. He will oversee complaint resolution, consumer protection, and service transparency.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Hotel Crowne Imperial to Offer 15% Discount, Promote Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with Hotel Crowne Imperial in Ravi Bhawan, Kathmandu, to offer its customers a 15% discount on accommodation, dining, drinks, and spa services when paying through digital channels such as debit/credit cards, prepaid cards, or the MoBank app. The collaboration aims to promote cashless transactions while enhancing customer experience.
The initiative supports Nepal’s digital economy by linking lifestyle services with modern payment methods, benefiting customers through savings and convenience, boosting the hotel’s patronage, and reinforcing the bank’s commitment to financial innovation and digital adoption.

Headline: NIC ASIA Bank Urges Customers to Update PAN and Email for Compliance and Digital Efficiency
Full Content:
NIC ASIA Bank has issued a public notice urging all customers to promptly update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) and email address. The bank emphasized that the PAN update is a mandatory legal requirement under the Income Tax Act, 2058, ensuring proper recording of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) in Nepal’s electronic tax system (E-TDS). This update enables automated tax matching, easy access to tax certificates, and compliance assurance.
Failure to update may cause discrepancies in customers’ tax records, for which the bank will not be held responsible. Alongside PAN updates, customers are encouraged to update their email addresses to enhance digital communication, receive e-statements, and ensure secure banking.
To simplify the process, the bank offers multiple update options, via its online portal, MoBank mobile app, Video KYC system, or any branch nationwide. The initiative reflects NIC ASIA’s commitment to combining regulatory compliance with customer convenience and digital transformation.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with The Cliff Nepal to Offer 10% Discount on Services
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed an agreement with The Cliff Nepal in Kusma, Parbat, allowing the bank’s customers to enjoy a 10% discount on various services, including accommodation, Skycycle, and Sky Café, when paying digitally.
Customers can avail the offer using NIC Asia debit, credit, or prepaid cards or through the MoBank app. The partnership aims to promote digital payments and support cashless transactions while providing added benefits to the bank’s customers.

Headline: Sujit Kumar Shakya Assumes Office as CEO of NIC Asia Bank
Full Content:
Sujit Kumar Shakya has officially assumed his role as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NIC Asia Bank Limited on Kartik 20, 2082, following the decision of the bank’s 736th Board meeting on Kartik 17, 2082.
With nearly three decades of experience in Nepal’s banking sector, Shakya holds a B.Com from Delhi University and an MBA from the Institute of Productivity and Management, Lucknow, India. He began his banking career in 1996 at the former Nepal Sri Lanka Merchant Bank and has since held key roles in Himalayan Bank, Laxmi Bank, Bank of Asia Nepal, and other leading banks. He played a pivotal role in the merger of Bank of Asia Nepal and NIC Bank, subsequently serving as Assistant General Manager and Head of Corporate Banking at NIC Asia Bank.
Before his CEO appointment, Shakya was Senior Deputy CEO at Nabil Bank and had also served as Deputy CEO at Civil Bank, Janata Bank, and Global IME Bank. Known for his analytical skills, strategic vision, and extensive banking experience, Shakya is expected to lead NIC Asia Bank toward greater growth, reliability, and industry prestige.

Headline: Sujit Kumar Shakya Appointed as New CEO of NIC Asia Bank
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has officially appointed Mr. Sujit Kumar Shakya as its new Chief Executive Officer for a tenure of four years. The decision was taken during the bank’s 736th Board of Directors meeting held on 2082/07/17.
Mr. Shakya, a resident of Pulchowk, Ward No. 3, Lalitpur Metropolitan City, brings over 28 years of extensive experience in the banking sector. He currently serves as the Senior Deputy Chief Executive Officer at Nabil Bank Ltd., where he also holds the position of Chairman.
He holds a Post Graduate Diploma in Business Management from the Institute of Productivity Management, India, and a Bachelor of Commerce (Honors) degree from Delhi University. Known for his strategic insight and leadership excellence, Mr. Shakya is expected to drive NIC Asia Bank toward continued growth and innovation in the financial sector.
As per the agreement, Mr. Shakya will assume office within the next 30 days, following which further details regarding his tenure will be officially shared.

Headline: Dividend Spotlight: A Closer Look into Dividend Declarations by Companies Across All Sectors for FY 2081/82
Full Content:
A number of companies listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) have declared dividends for their shareholders for fiscal year 2081/82, reflecting their financial performance and commitment to investor returns. The announcements cover a broad range of sectors, with dividend distributions seen across Banking, Development Bank, Finance, Hotels and Tourism, Hydropower, Investment, Manufacturing and Processing, Microfinance, and Mutual Fund categories. These declarations include both cash and bonus shares, highlighting the varying strategies companies have adopted to reward their investors.
Meanwhile, four sectors, Life Insurance, Non-Life Insurance, Others, and Trading, have not declared any dividends this year. This contrast underscores the differing profitability levels and market conditions across industries within NEPSE. The overall dividend landscape offers valuable insights into the strength and stability of Nepal’s listed companies, serving as a key indicator for investor confidence and sectoral performance in the current fiscal period.
The following data presents a detailed breakdown of all the companies from each sector that have declared dividends this fiscal year:
Commercial Banks
The table below presents the list of commercial banks listed under the Banking Index that have declared dividends this fiscal year, along with details on bonus shares, cash dividends, AGM dates, and book closure dates.
Out of the 19 commercial banks listed under the Banking Index, only seven have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Everest Bank (EBL) declared the highest total dividend among commercial banks, distributing 20% in total, comprising 6% bonus shares and a 14% cash dividend.
Development Banks
Out of the 16 development banks listed under the Development Bank Index, only four have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) distributed the highest total dividend of 18.20%, including 13.53% bonus shares and a 4.67% cash dividend.
In contrast, Miteri Development Bank (MDB) declared the lowest dividend among development banks, offering only a 10% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Finance
Only one finance company, Manjushree Finance (MFIL), has declared a dividend for FY 2081/82. The company announced a 15% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Hotels and Tourism
From the Hotel and Tourism sector, only Soaltee Hotel (SHL) announced the total dividend of 31.5789%, comprising 15% bonus shares and a 16.5789% cash dividend.
Hydropower
Among the 94 hydropower companies listed under the Hydropower Index, only five have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Bhagawati Hydropower Development Company (BGWT) distributed the highest total dividend of 20%, comprising 14% bonus shares and a 6% cash dividend.
At the lower end, Arun Valley Hydropower Development Company (AHPC) announced a total dividend of 8.421%, including 8% bonus shares and a 0.421% cash dividend. The overall declarations from the sector suggest selective profitability, with only a handful of hydropower companies managing to reward shareholders this fiscal year.
Investment
Out of seven companies in the sector, only Hathway Investment Nepal (HATHY) and Nepal Infrastructure Bank (NIFRA) have announced dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Hathway Investment has declared a total dividend of 12.632%, including a 12% bonus share and 0.632% cash dividend. The company’s AGM was scheduled for Bhadra 25, 2082, with the book closure date on Bhadra 13, 2082.
Nepal Infrastructure Bank has declared a 6.3158% cash dividend, without issuing bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for NIFRA have not yet been announced.
Manufacturing and Processing
In the Manufacturing sector, only Himalayan Distillery (HDL), Nepal Lube Oil (NLO), and Unilever Nepal (UNL) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Himalayan Distillery has announced a total dividend of 25%, including a 20% bonus share and 5% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 30, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 20, 2082.
Nepal Lube Oil declared a total dividend of 21.05264%, comprising a 20% bonus share and 1.05264% cash dividend. The AGM was set for Ashwin 31, 2082, with the book closure date on Ashwin 12, 2082.
Unilever Nepal announced a cash dividend of 1842%, with no bonus shares. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 25, 2082, and the book closure period is Kartik 11–25, 2082.
Microfinance
In the Microfinance sector, only Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (GLBSL) and RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (RSDC) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha has announced a total dividend of 15%, consisting of a 14.25% bonus share and 0.75% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 23, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 14, 2082.
RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha declared an 8% cash dividend, with no bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for RSDC have not yet been announced.
Mutual Fund
All 52 mutual funds have declared cash dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82. Notable funds include Laxmi Unnati Kosh (20%), Sanima Large Cap Fund (21.05%), Siddhartha Equity Fund (20%), RBB Mutual Fund 1 (20%), and Sunrise Bluechip Fund (19%). Other funds have announced dividends between 5% and 20%.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Requests Customers to Update PAN for Tax Compliance
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank urges its customers to update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) to comply with Nepal’s Income Tax Act, 2058. Customers can update their PAN through the bank’s portal (panupdate.nicasiabank.com), mobile banking app (NIC ASIA MoBank), or by visiting any branch.
Updating PAN is essential for recording tax deducted at source (E-TDS) on interest payments. Once updated, E-TDS details will automatically match with Income Tax schedules, simplifying the issuance of Tax Deduction and Tax Clearance Certificates. The bank clarified it will not be responsible if the interest tax is not reported due to a customer’s failure to update the PAN. Customers facing issues even after providing PAN are advised to contact the nearest branch or the customer service center at 1660-01-77771 / 01-5970101.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Shrawan; GBIME Tops the Charts
Full Content:

Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 15.72 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 13.39 Crores in net profit. Lumbini Bikas Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 11.08 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Saptakoshi Development Bank and Salapa Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 32.4 lakhs and Rs. 6.9 lakhs, respectively.
Furthermore, five banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Bhadra Interest Rate Update: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates; Majority Keep Rates Unchanged
Full Content:
Commercial banks have announced their revised fixed deposit (FD) interest rates for the month of Bhadra. Out of the 20 commercial banks, 11 left their rates unchanged from Shrawan, while nine made adjustments. Among them, eight banks lowered their rates, whereas one opted for an increase.
Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) implemented the sharpest reduction in institutional FD rates, trimming them by 1.13 percentage points—from 6.26% in Shrawan to 5.13% in Bhadra. Similarly, Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) cut its institutional FD rate by 0.75 percentage points, bringing it down to 4% from 4.75% in the previous month.
On the other hand, Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) stood out as the only bank to increase rates, raising its institutional FD rate by 1.10 percentage points—from 4.25% in Shrawan to 5.35% in Bhadra.
In terms of prevailing rates, Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) offers the lowest individual FD rate at 5%, while Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) provides the lowest institutional FD rate at 2.75%. At the higher end, NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) leads with the highest rates, offering 6.25% for individual FDs and 5.25% for institutional FDs.

Headline: Unveiling Q4 2081/82: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the fourth quarter of FY 2081/82, offering a fresh look into their performance during the twelve-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q4 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 7.13 Arba, marking a 15.01% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 6.76 Arba, though this represents a 64.46% increase from the previous year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 6.20 Arba.
Kumari Bank Limited (NBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 45280.14% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 77.03%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.69 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 18.46 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 37.78 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 36.68 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 33.23 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 64.43 Kharba in customer deposits, with eight banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.50 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.24 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 5 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.25 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.13 Kharba, followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) with Rs. 4.12 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 72.21 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.33 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 16.71 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 16.33 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 25.52 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 4.31 Arba, with NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) next at Rs. 4.14 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 37.99, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 27.63 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 26.34. The industry average EPS was Rs. 18.44, with ten banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 1.08.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 38.27 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.47. Four banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 341.59, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 259.81 and Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 243.40. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 142.19, while the industry average stood at Rs. 201.57.
*Note: Preference Share is excluded while calculating the Net worth of Agriculture Development Bank (ADBL).
P/E Ratio:
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) had the lowest P/E ratio at 9.60 times, followed by  Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at 11.35 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.82%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the lowest at 11.64%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.38%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.28%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 1.95% while
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest
ROE at 15.36%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.21%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.22%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 84.33%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 62.39%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.04%, and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 4.89%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.6% to 3.9%.
The table below provides a detailed overview of these financial indicators across the 20 commercial banks for Q4 FY 2081/82.

Headline: Commercial Banks Post Rs. 71.50 Arba Net Profit in Q4 FY 2081/82; Nabil Bank Leads Net Profit, Everest Bank Tops Distributable Profit Per Share
Full Content:
Nepal’s commercial banks have reported their net profits for the fourth quarter (Q4) of FY 2081-82, based on unaudited financial statements.
Net Profit:
Collectively, the 20 commercial banks posted a net profit of Rs. 71.50 Arba, reflecting a 43.39% year-on-year (YoY) growth compared to Rs. 49.86 Arba in the same period of FY 2080/81.
Nabil Bank Limited recorded the highest net profit, earning Rs. 7.13 Arba by the end of Ashad, a 15.01% increase from the previous year. Following Nabil, Nepal Investment Mega Bank posted Rs. 6.76 Arba, while Global IME Bank earned Rs. 6.20 Arba. NIC Asia Bank recorded the lowest net profit at Rs. 16 crores, experiencing the steepest YoY decline of 77.03% from Rs. 70 crores in FY 2080/81.
Kumari Bank reported the highest profit growth among all banks, with an increase of 45,820.14%. Other banks showing notable growth after revising previous year figures include Prabhu Bank and Nepal Bank.
However, four banks—Standard Chartered Bank, Nepal SBI Bank, Citizens Bank International, and NIC Asia Bank—recorded a decline in profit during the review period, with NIC Asia Bank’s net profit falling the most.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
In terms of distributable profit per share, Everest Bank Limited (EBL) led with Rs. 38.27 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.47. Despite being second in total net profit, Nepal Investment Mega Bank reported the lowest distributable profit per share at Rs. 1.44. Four banks recorded negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.

Customers using CG internet plans of 150 Mbps, 250 Mbps, and 350 Mbps are eligible for the NPR 2,500 discount annually, which also applies to new IPTV subscribers. Existing customers renewing their service will receive an additional month free annually. To avail these benefits, customers must contact CG Communications through their official phone number, website, or branch offices before subscribing. This partnership aims to enhance internet accessibility, promote digital payment services, and support cashless transactions across Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Urges Customers to Update PAN for Seamless Tax Deduction and Certification
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank, serving millions of customers with dynamic banking services, has requested all account holders to update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) as mandated by Nepal’s Income Tax Act, 2058. This update ensures proper recording of tax deductions (E-TDS) under the government’s tax system. Customers can update their PAN easily through the bank’s portal (panupdate.nicasiabank.com), mobile app (NIC ASIA MoBank), or by visiting any bank branch.
Updating PAN will enable automatic matching of tax deductions, facilitating easier issuance of tax deduction and clearance certificates, and eliminating the need for customers to visit the bank repeatedly. The bank also clarified that it is not responsible for any tax adjustments arising from non-updated PAN details. Customers facing issues can contact nearby branches or call the bank’s customer support for assistance.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Offers 10% Discount at Himalaya Drishya Resort to Boost Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with Himalaya Drishya Resort in Dhulikhel to offer a 10% discount on food and beverages for customers using the bank’s digital payment channels (debit/credit/prepaid cards or MoBank app).
This collaboration promotes cashless transactions, enhances customer experience, and supports Nepal’s digital economy and domestic tourism.
The resort offers stunning Himalayan views and top-tier hospitality, making the offer attractive for leisure seekers. The bank aims to expand such lifestyle partnerships, aligning with national goals of financial inclusion and digital transformation.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Let Mein Korean Skin Hospital to Offer Special Discounts to Customers
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with Let Mein Korean Skin Hospital, operating in New Baneshwor, Maharajgunj, and Pokhara (Chipledhunga), to offer exclusive discounts to its customers.
Clients using the bank’s debit, credit, prepaid cards, or MoBank app for digital payments can receive up to 10% off on services such as hair transplants, facials, anti-aging, acne, scar treatments, and oxygen therapy, along with 8% off on Korean products. The initiative aims to promote both customer benefits and digital payment adoption in Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Partners with Lemon Tree Premier to Offer Exclusive Discounts and Boost Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed an agreement with Budhanilkantha Heritage Ltd. to offer special discounts to its customers at Lemon Tree Premier, Budhanilkantha.
Under the partnership, customers using the bank’s digital payment methods (debit card, credit card, prepaid card, or MoBank app) can receive up to a 20% discount, 15% on accommodation, food, and beverages, and 20% on spa services.
The agreement was signed by Bimal Lamsal from NIC Asia and Manoj Kumar Thapa from Budhanilkantha Heritage Ltd. The collaboration aims to enhance customer benefits while promoting digital payment practices in Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Kantipur Dental to Offer Exclusive Health Discounts and Boost Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has agreed with Kantipur Dental College Teaching Hospital and Research Center (KDC) to offer special discounts on dental and health services to its customers. Under this partnership, NIC Asia customers can receive up to a 15% discount when paying digitally at various KDC branches.
Discounts include 15% on general hospital services (such as lab tests and ICU), 10% on physiotherapy, eyeglasses, and general dental services (like filling, scaling, RCT), and 7% on advanced dental procedures (like implants, braces, and veneers).
The discounts are available at KDC Aesthetic Center in Jorpati, Kathmandu, Kantipur Institute of Health Sciences in Pokhara, and KDC branches in Satungal (Kathmandu), Bharatpur (Chitwan), and Bhallwari Tilottama (Butwal).
To avail the offer, customers must use NIC Asia’s debit/credit/prepaid cards or the MoBank app. The bank believes this initiative promotes both health service affordability and digital payment adoption across Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Introduces Share-Backed Loan Scheme with 8.17% Interest Rate, Offering Up to Rs. 15 Crore
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has launched a new loan product titled
‘NIC Asia ATHOT Loan Against Share’
, offering financing against shares at a competitive interest rate of 8.17%, calculated as the base rate plus a 1% premium. The scheme is designed to support investors in the capital market by providing accessible credit backed by shares listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange, including those of banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies.
Under this facility, customers can receive loans of up to 70% of the lower value between the average market price over 180 days or the most recent transaction price of their pledged shares. The loan amount ranges from a minimum of Rs. 50 lakh to a maximum of Rs. 15 crore. The product aims to address the evolving financial needs of share investors with a quick and efficient approval process.
NIC Asia Bank has committed to disbursing the loan within three working days after receiving all required documents. To further streamline services, the bank has set up a dedicated Loan Support Center to provide expert advice, handle customer inquiries, and resolve complaints promptly through a single-window approach.

Headline: NIC ASIA Bank Partners with Hair n Shanti Salon to Offer 10% Digital Payment Discount
Full Content:
NIC ASIA Bank has partnered with Liza Shree Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. to offer a 10% discount to its customers at Hair n Shanti Unisex Salon branches across Nepal.
Customers can avail the discount by making payments via NIC ASIA’s debit, credit, or prepaid cards, or through the MoBank app. This collaboration aims to promote digital payments while providing value-added services to customers.

Full Content:

Customers can avail the discount by using NIC Asia’s debit, credit, or prepaid cards, or through the MoBank app. The partnership aims to enhance access to digital payments in healthcare and promote the use of digital financial services across Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Partners with ASG Eye Care to Offer Exclusive Discounts and Promote Digital Health Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed an agreement with ASG Eye Care and Health Services Pvt. Ltd. to offer special discounts on eye treatment services to its customers. These include up to NPR 10,000 off on surgeries, 10% off on minor investigations and optical/lens services, and free OPD and registration fees for first-time patients. This collaboration aims to expand digital payment adoption in healthcare and enhance accessible, quality eye care across Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Celebrates 28 Years of Trust, Innovation, and Nationwide Financial Inclusion
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank celebrates its 28th anniversary, marking its journey from inception to becoming one of Nepal's most trusted, dynamic, and customer-centric banks. The bank expresses gratitude to customers, regulators, shareholders, and employees for their continued support.
Committed to becoming a world-class, tech-friendly bank of choice, NIC Asia has expanded its reach with 360 branches, 670 ATMs, and services in even the most remote districts. It continues to lead in digital banking, financial inclusion, and economic contribution across Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Om Hospital to Offer 10% Discount on Digital Payments
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has signed an agreement with Om Hospital & Research Centre Pvt. Ltd. to offer a 10% discount on medical treatment for its customers who make digital payments.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Director Ram Chandra Sanghai Honored with CIP Award
Full Content:
Mr. Ram Chandra Sanghai, a director of NIC Asia Bank, has been honored with the prestigious Commercially Important Person (CIP) award by the Government of Nepal.

The government annually bestows the CIP title on individuals who have made notable impacts on the country’s economic development. NIC Asia Bank extends heartfelt congratulations to Mr. Sanghai on receiving this distinguished honor.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Launches Online Auction Portal for Asset Sales
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has launched a new online portal to provide comprehensive information about properties up for auction, including banking and non-banking assets as well as collateral-held properties.
Accessible via QR codes on auction notices or directly at
https://auctionassistance.nicasiabank.com
, the portal offers details such as plot numbers, area, photos, maps, and Google Maps-based location info.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Partners with Nagarkot Homestay to Offer Digital Payment Discounts
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with Nagarkot Community Homestay to offer a 10% discount to its customers on digital payments made through the bank’s mobile banking app (MoBank).
This offer is valid at the homestay operated by 17 families in Changunarayan, Bhaktapur. The collaboration aims to promote digital payments and support sustainable rural tourism while enhancing financial inclusion and digital empowerment.

Headline: NIC Asia Partners with E. Stop Nepal to Boost Green Economy with Exclusive EV and Dining Discounts
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has partnered with E. Stop Nepal Pvt. Ltd. to offer exclusive discounts to its customers on restaurant meals and EV charging services.
Under the agreement, customers will receive a 10% discount on food and a 5% discount on charging services at E. Stop Nepal locations in Daldale (Nawalpur), Ramtar (Sindhuli), and Kurintar.
These benefits are available when payments are made using NIC Asia debit, credit, or prepaid cards, or via the MoBank app. The bank believes this collaboration supports digital payments and promotes a green economy in Nepal.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Urges Customers to Update PAN for Tax Compliance
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank requests its customers to update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) in their accounts as mandated by Nepal’s Income Tax Act. Customers can update their PAN via the bank’s portal, mobile app, or any branch.
Updating PAN is Electronic Tax Deducted at source (E-TDS) reporting on interest payments, enabling smooth issuance of tax deduction and clearance certificates.
The bank is not responsible if customers fail to update their PAN, causing tax reporting issues. Customers facing issues despite submitting their PAN should contact the nearest branch or customer service.

Headline: NIC ASIA Bank Empowers Global Tourists with NepalPay QR via Alipay+ Integration
Full Content:
NIC ASIA Bank has partnered with Nepal Clearing House Limited (NCHL) to enable international tourists using the Alipay+ network to make direct payments at NepalPay QR-enabled merchants in Nepal.
This integration allows travelers from over 11 countries, including China, Malaysia, Thailand, and Germany, to use their native digital wallets or banking apps for seamless transactions while visiting Nepal.
Signed by senior officials of both institutions, the agreement enhances cross-border QR payment capabilities, simplifying the payment experience for tourists and expanding opportunities for local businesses connected with NIC ASIA Bank.
As one of Nepal’s leading commercial banks, NIC ASIA offers extensive digital banking services, with over 300 branches and advanced tools like the MoBank app. Known for innovation, the bank also maintains a strong commitment to security and social responsibility.

Headline: SEBON Approves NIC Asia Capital’s Mutual Fund Scheme "NIC ASIA Equity Linked Investment Scheme" To Issue 10 Crore Units
Full Content:
The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) has approved the
"NIC ASIA Equity Linked Investment Scheme"
worth Rs 1 Arba on Ashadh 03, 2082.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Baisakh; NABIL Tops the Charts Once More
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for till the tenth month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Baisakh.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 47.79 Arba. Nabil Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 5.6 Arba, overtaking Global IME Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 5.35 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 5.02 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the NIC Asia Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 47.87 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 4.59 Arba, despite five out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 87.68 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank which posted Rs. 86.93 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 61.54 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Green Development Bank and Corporate Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 2.32 crores and Rs. 1.56 crores, respectively.
Furthermore, eight banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Salapa, Corporate Development Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Relocates Corporate Office to Newly Constructed Building in Kamaladi
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has officially relocated its corporate office to its newly constructed building located in Kamaladi, Kathmandu Metropolitan City Ward No. 28. The move was made effective from Jestha 10, 2082 (May 24, 2025), following approval from Nepal Rastra Bank on Jestha 9, 2082 (May 23, 2025).
Until now, the bank's corporate office had been operating from Trade Tower Nepal in Thapathali, Ward No. 11 of Kathmandu Metropolitan City. The relocation to Kamaladi marks a significant milestone for NIC Asia Bank, as it now operates from a building owned and built by the bank itself, enhancing its infrastructure and operational capacity.
The management has formally notified the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) of this shift in location for official records and stakeholder awareness.
NIC ASIA Bank continues to strengthen its presence and services across Nepal, with this relocation symbolizing its commitment to long-term growth and service excellence.

Headline: NIC ASIA Bank’s Innovative Online Auction Portal Enhances Transparency and Convenience
Full Content:
NIC ASIA Bank has launched a new online auction portal that provides detailed information about properties for sale, including banking and non-banking assets. The portal allows users to access property details easily via QR code, view photos, maps, and contact the bank directly for more information.
This digital platform enhances transparency, convenience, and efficiency in property auctions, reflecting the bank’s commitment to smart banking and service automation. The portal is regularly updated, user-friendly, and aims to help buyers make informed decisions while setting a new standard for digital services in Nepal’s banking sector.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates for Jestha: NIMB Slashes, SANIMA Leads the Hike
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published their revised fixed deposit (FD) interest rates for the month of Jestha. While most banks have kept their rates unchanged compared to the previous month of Baisakh, a few have made adjustments.
Out of the 20 commercial banks, 14 banks maintained the same interest rates as in Baisakh, whereas the remaining 6 banks revised their rates, with three banks decreasing and three increasing their rates.
Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) made the steepest cut, reducing its individual fixed deposit rate by 1 percentage point, from 6.50% in Baisakh to 5.50% in Jestha.
Similarly, Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) lowered its rate by 0.25 percentage points, and Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) made a slight decrease of 0.01 percentage points.
Among the banks that increased individual FD rates, Sanima Bank Limited (SANIMA) led with a rise of 0.38 percentage points.
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) followed with a 0.30 percentage point increase, while Everest Bank Limited (EBL) saw a marginal hike of 0.03 percentage points.
Additionally, Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) increased its institutional fixed deposit rate by 1 percentage point, from 3.00% to 4.00%.

Headline: Delving into Q3 2081/82: Performance Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks with Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the third quarter of FY 2081/82, offering a fresh look into their performance during the nine-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q3 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 5.05 Arba, marking an 8.21% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 4.54 Arba, though this represents a 38.61% increase from the previous year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 4.53 Arba.
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 2032.94% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 91.81%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.41 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 17.07 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 36.38 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 34.19 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 30.85 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 60.35 Kharba in customer deposits, with eight banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.18 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.02 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 4.01 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 77.26 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.31 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 12.32 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 12.05 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 35.07 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 5.17 Arba, with Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) next at Rs. 3.20 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 35.61, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at Rs. 28.86 and Nepal Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 25.26. The industry average EPS was Rs. 15.12, with eleven banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 1.40.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 28.42 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 16.19. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 332.66, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 264.85 and Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 260.74. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 134.43, with the industry average at Rs. 195.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) had the lowest P/E ratio at 9.94 times, followed by  Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at 11.92 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.44%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the lowest at 10.84%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.64%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.68%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 1.92% while
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest
ROE at 16.10%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.47%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.3%.
- CD Ratio:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) had the highest CD ratio at 85.90%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 64.37%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.20%, and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 5.02%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.8% to 4%.
The table below provides a detailed overview of these financial indicators across the 20 commercial banks for Q3 FY 2081/82.
**Note: All figures are reported in Arba except for net profit, which is presented in crores for clarity.

Headline: Commercial Banks' Net Profits Rise by 1.40% in Q3; Nepal Bank Sees Over 2000% Surge, NIC Asia Suffers 91% Decline
Full Content:
Nepal's commercial banks have reported their net profits for the third quarter of the current fiscal year, according to their unaudited financial statements. The collective net profit of the 20 commercial banks stood at Rs. 41.25 Arba, marking a modest 1.40% year-on-year (YoY) growth compared to Rs. 40.68 Arba recorded during the same period in fiscal year 2080/81.
The most remarkable performance was delivered by Nepal Bank, which reported a net profit of Rs. 278.35 crores, a dramatic leap from just Rs. 13.05 crores in the same quarter last year. This translates to a staggering 2032.94% increase, making it the highest percentage growth among all commercial banks this quarter.
Strong performances were also seen from several other institutions. Nepal Investment Mega Bank posted a net profit of Rs. 454 crores, rising by 38.61% from the previous year. Similarly, Global IME Bank earned Rs. 453.41 crores, up 37.12%, while Everest Bank and Machhapuchchhre Bank posted profits of Rs. 345.76 crores and Rs. 110.26 crores, registering growths of 32.55% and 28.90% respectively.
Moderate profit growth was reported by banks like Sanima Bank (14.80%), Nabil Bank (8.21%), NMB Bank (5.87%), Prabhu Bank (3.51%), and Nepal SBI Bank (3.36%). Laxmi Sunrise Bank also posted a small increase of 2.24% in net profit.

Headline: NIC Asia Launches New Year 2082 Offer: Chance to Win iPhone 16 via MoBank

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Limited Opening the Issue of "7% NIC Asia Debenture 2091" From Today
Full Content:

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Urges Customers to Update PAN for Tax Compliance
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank has requested its customers to update their Permanent Account Numbers (PANs) to comply with the Income Tax Act 2058. Customers can update their PAN via the bank’s portal
(panupdate.nicasiabank.com)

Updating the PAN ensures that tax deductions (E-TDS) on interest payments are properly recorded, facilitating the automatic reconciliation of tax details in Schedule 10 of the tax system. The bank clarified that if customers fail to update their PAN, interest tax deposits may not be recorded, and the bank will not be responsible for any required adjustments. Customers facing issues can contact customer support at 1660-01-77771 or 01-5970101 for assistance.

Headline: Performance Analysis of A-Class Banks in Q2 2081/82: Key Financial Metrics and Insights
Full Content:
The release of the second-quarter financial reports for FY 2081/82 by all 20 commercial banks sheds light on their financial performance, offering a detailed view of profitability, business volume, and key financial metrics. This analysis covers the second-quarter results, highlighting trends across net profit, capital adequacy, and other pivotal indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q2 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 3.24 Arba, marking a 1.29% increase over the same period last year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) followed with a net profit of Rs. 3.05 Arba, though this represents a 49.51% incline from the previous year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) took third with Rs. 2.83 Arba.
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 85.50% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 92.03%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.28 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 16.41 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 35.94 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 32.02 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 29.03 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 58.91 Kharba in customer deposits, with ten banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 4.8 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.47 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.07 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 3.91 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 78.17 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.27 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 8.30 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 7.9 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 24.67 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 3.27 Arba, with Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) next at Rs. 2.53 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 32.67, followed by Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 32.06 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 23.98. The industry average EPS was Rs. 14.72, with nine banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 2.03.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 20.99 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 13.25. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 329.84, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 261.96 and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 225.79. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 133.51, with the industry average at Rs. 190.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) had the lowest P/E ratio at 12.71 times, followed by Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at 12.81 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 16.94%, with Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) at 13.26%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.66%, while Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) reported the highest NPL at 6.96%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 2.16% and ROE at 16.10%. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with strong performances.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.69%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.38%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 86.76%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 63.20%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.52%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the lowest at 5.13%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.96% to 4%.

Headline: Commercial Banks Report 4.62% Decline in Net Profit for Q2 FY 2081/82; NABIL Leads, Prabhu Bank Sees Highest Growth
Full Content:
Nepal's commercial banks have reported a decrease in net profits for the second quarter of the current fiscal year, according to their unaudited financial statements. As of the end of Poush (mid-January), the 20 commercial banks collectively earned a net profit of Rs. 27.43 Arba, marking a 4.62% drop compared to the Rs. 28.76 Arba earned during the same period last year.
Out of the 20 banks, 9 recorded a decrease in net profits, contributing to the overall decline. However, 11 banks experienced growth in their earnings. Among these, Prabhu Bank stood out with the highest increase in net profit, reporting an impressive 85.49% rise. The bank's net profit surged from Rs. 72.03 Crores last year to Rs. 133.61 Crores this year. Similarly, Nepal Investment Mega Bank saw an increase of over 57.18%, while Global IME Bank's profit grew by 49.51%, and NMB Bank's profit rose by 45.61%.
On the other hand, NIC Asia Bank experienced the steepest drop in net profit, with a staggering 92.03% decrease. The bank’s profit plummeted from Rs. 1.90 Arba last year to just Rs. 15.17 Crores this year. Kumari Bank also saw a significant decline in net profit, falling by over 68.20%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank’s profit dropped by more than 62.14%.
Nabil Bank recorded the highest net profit for the quarter, amounting to Rs. 3.24 Arba, which marks a modest 1.29% increase from the same period last year. Global IME Bank also posted a strong performance, reporting a net profit exceeding Rs. 3 Arba.
During the second quarter, 11 commercial banks surpassed the Rs. 1 Arba mark in net profits. Among them, two banks reported more than Rs. 3 Arba in net profit, while three banks earned over Rs. 2 Arba. The remaining six banks each posted profits exceeding Rs. 1 Arba. Despite the overall decline in profits, the banking sector remains an important player in Nepal's financial landscape, with some institutions continuing to demonstrate significant growth.

Headline: NIC Asia Bank Urges Elite Customers to Update Permanent Account Numbers
Full Content:
NIC Asia Bank is requesting its elite customers to update their Permanent Account Number (PAN) in their accounts.
This update is required to comply with the "Income Tax Act 2058," which mandates entering tax deduction details into the PAN system managed by the Government of Nepal's Internal Revenue Department.
Customers can update their PAN through the bank's portal (panupdate.nicasiabank.com) or mobile banking app (NIC ASIA MoBank) by selecting the "PAN Update" option. Additionally, customers can apply for PAN renewal at any bank branch.
Updating the PAN will ensure that tax deduction details are accurately recorded, simplifying the process of obtaining tax certificates and avoiding issues related to E-TDS records.
The bank disclaims responsibility for any issues arising from the failure to update the PAN and advises contacting the nearest branch or customer contact center if PAN details are not reflected correctly.

Headline: Commercial Banks Reduce Base Interest Rates to 7.92% Amid Surplus Loanable Funds
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have reduced their average base interest rate to 7.92% for the period between mid-August and mid-September, driven by an excess of loanable funds. This marks a 0.25 percentage point decrease compared to the previous months, signaling a potential reduction in lending rates in the near future.
According to reports from the 20 commercial banks, Standard Chartered Bank has set the lowest base rate at 6.22%, followed by state-owned Rastriya Banijya Bank with a rate of 6.66%. On the higher end, NIC Asia Bank maintains the highest base rate at 9.22%, while Kumari Bank follows closely with 8.90%.
Over the past few months, banks have been gradually lowering their interest rates, with the average base rate consistently remaining in single digits since May 2024.
The lending rate of a bank is determined by adding a premium to its base rate, which typically ranges from 1.5% to 5%, depending on the nature of the loan and associated risks.
The reduction in base rates comes amid an economic slowdown, rising non-performing assets (NPAs), and challenges related to capital adequacy ratios. However, banks have shown improvement in key areas, including increased lending for auto loans and loans secured against shares as collateral. Records from Nepal Rastra Bank also reveal that banks have reduced a portion of their NPAs while strengthening their capital adequacy positions.
As lending rates are likely to follow the downward trend in base rates, businesses and individuals may benefit from more affordable loan opportunities in the coming months.
